---
description: world_path as the model is told it - what the tool does, and what each of its arguments is.
arguments:
  from: "One end of the way, by name or id."
  to: "The other end."
  mode: "walk, road, offroad, water or air; left out, walk."
  minutes: "How long it takes by that mode, in minutes; needed to lay a way."
  km: "How far it is by that mode, in kilometres."
  terrain: "What it crosses, in a word."
  one_way: "true to make the way run from the first place to the second only; false to make it run both ways."
  remove: "true to take the way out, or, with a mode, that mode of it."
  source: "Where it comes from: from is prose, lore, author, gm, character, player, default or invented; lore, message and roll cite an entry, a message or a roll by id; an invention cites its gap_check and consent."
  precision: "How exact: exact, approximate, vague or unknown."
  standing: "How it stands: established, proposed or assumed."
---
Lays, changes or takes out a way between two places in this chat, with its minutes and distance by each way of travel. Laying a way needs its minutes; changing one needs only what changes. A way a map draws is changed in the map. The answer says what changed.
